title: Connect your web application to Frontend Observability

blocks.content: Create a Frontend Observability application and get AI-assisted Faro setup instructions. You need permission to create applications and access to your frontend code; deployment happens after this guide.

blocks.prompt: What origin serves your website? Include http:// or https:// and a port if needed, without a path.

blocks.content: An application groups the telemetry from one frontend. To create yours, complete the following steps:
Open **AI assisted** setup in **Frontend Observability**.
blocks.tooltip: Start the web application wizard with AI-assisted instrumentation.

blocks.content: Enter your own **Application name**, such as `my-web-app`.

steps.formHint: Enter a descriptive name for your application or check.
steps.tooltip: Use a name that distinguishes this frontend from other applications and environments.
steps.description: Enter your own **Application name**, such as `my-web-app`.

blocks.content: Set **Allowed origins** to {{appUrl}}.
blocks.tooltip: Use the exact scheme, hostname, and port your visitors use; add other environments separately.

blocks.reftarget: #pageContent:has(h1:contains('Create a Frontend Observability web application')) button:contains('Next')
blocks.content: Click **Next** to create the application. If an error appears, correct it and try again.
blocks.tooltip: The next stage appears only after the application is saved.

blocks.content: Confirm that **Instrument with AI** opens for your new application.
blocks.tooltip: The application is saved; instrumentation and deployment still come next.

blocks.content: Your application is saved with its allowed origin; it will receive browser telemetry after you instrument and deploy your frontend.
Choose an AI agent to prepare the Faro instrumentation for your application.
Choose **Claude Code skill**, **Cursor skill**, or **Grafana Assistant** if available. Use the tool you already work with; choosing Grafana Assistant opens its chat.
blocks.tooltip: Choose your own agent; review and approve any proposed code changes.

blocks.content: Review your selected tool’s instructions and application-specific collector URL, or continue in the Grafana Assistant chat. Add Faro to your code and deploy the changes after this guide.
blocks.tooltip: These instructions belong to your new application; opening them does not mean it is sending telemetry.

blocks.content: You have the instructions for your application; review and deploy the generated changes after setup.
Source maps are optional; continue past them to finish the initial setup.
Click **Next** to continue to the optional source-map setup.
blocks.tooltip: You can finish setup before deploying the instrumentation.

blocks.content: Source maps are optional. Leave them for later to finish the initial setup.
blocks.tooltip: You can add source maps later to make production stack traces readable.

blocks.content: You can add source maps later to make production stack traces readable.
Finish setup and open your application’s overview.
Click **Complete setup** to open your application.
blocks.tooltip: This finishes configuration without requiring a source-map upload or incoming data.

blocks.content: Confirm that your application’s **Overview** opens. It may have no data until you deploy Faro and visit your website.
blocks.tooltip: Check this application after deployment; data from another application does not confirm it is connected.

blocks.content: The application is configured. Deploy the Faro SDK, then visit your website and use it to generate browser telemetry.
After deployment, check this application’s recent sessions and errors. If it remains empty, check the collector URL, allowed origin, and browser network errors.
